newsitem.title: UK: Euro monetary union could make or break banks - IBM.
newsitem.headline: Euro monetary union could make or break banks - IBM.

text.p: European Monetary Union could pose great threats or offer a potential opportunity to the banking sector, research commissioned by IBM and released in a report on Wednesday shows.
"The transition to the Euro will intensify competition in an already overcrowded European marketplace," commented John Downe, IBM's EMU executive for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

"Banks must seize the initiative and leverage the opportunity to consolidate and increase their corporate business. If they do not they may become casualties in a post monetary union rationalisation."

The survey questioned 200 corporates in France, Italy, Germany, Spain and the UK. Fewer than half said they had been approached by their own banks with offers of services and advice in the run-up to monetary union.
But 28 percent of the largest corporates said they would reduce the number of banks they dealt with and 38 percent had been approached by new banks.

German banks had been most active approaching competitors' clients in their home markets and across European borders; 77 percent of corporates in Germany had been approached where only 27 percent of Italian corporates had been contacted by theirs.
The IBM report said most banks would have to be "considerably more pro-active" in their approach to monetary union if they wanted to retain satisfied clients.

During a dual currency period, 29 percent of respondents said they would want advice on updating procedures and systems. They were also interested in a shield from a dual currency, and accounts transferral between currencies.

The survey said there may also be a "significant marketing opportunity" for banks to approach medium sized companies, which may not have been tapped before but which would need even more help than larger corporates.
